name: Splitter Choss
text: [what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — optional for the approach
earlierWhy: why: Snow gear optional on approach; glacier not stated. | secondReview: unsure/unsure: Only optional crampons for the approach are mentioned and no source covered this line.

name: North Gully
text: [overview] Turning right gives the main gully, snow with WI2 steps to the top;
[overview] Descent options: by way of Thunder-East Glacier, steep creek, or downclimbing or rappelling the gully.
[detailed_rack] Ice screws, and perhaps a picket or two.
earlierWhy: why: Descent may use a glacier; the ascent line is snow gully.

name: West Ridge
text: [descent_text] From the summit, put on crampons and descend west on snow or ice until the scree slopes leading toward Twincicle Pass appear.
[descent_text] Go down through Twincicle Pass and the Twincicle Valley, which is a tangle of alders, and cross the short but very steep Twincicle Glacier.
earlierWhy: why: Descent crosses a short steep glacier.

name: West Twincil
text: [overview] alternatively stop above and climb a near-vertical snow step 10-20 ft tall to a ledge, from which a wider couloir continues to the basin below.
[detailed_rack] Steep snow and complex avalanche terrain;
[detailed_rack] consult snow and avalanche forecasts beforehand.
[approach] The line is steep, narrow and avalanche-prone, so it is best entered in very stable conditions after studying the map and the snow.
earlierWhy: why: Steep avalanche couloir; glacier not stated.

name: Gog East Face
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier.
[approach] Gog is the higher, closer-to-the-col summit of the Gog-Magog pair, and the route starts on its east face, reached by hiking across the snow below it and crossing the moat to the rock.
[descent_text] Cross the moat and walk down the snowfield toward the Friendship Col trail and the hut.
earlierWhy: why: It crosses a snowfield and a moat below the face; searches did not say whether the Echo Glacier side is crevassed.

name: Mount Quadrant West Face to North Summit (Stem-winder)
text: [overview] Snow may cover the approach and return.

[approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the Friendship Col trail until it turns up the snow slopes toward Gog and Magog, then continue straight over the ridge, drop down and around the left side of the lake, and climb back up to the base of Quadrant's north face.
[approach] There is some snow on the approach.
earlierWhy: why: The text only mentions some snow on the approach, and searches gave no detail on its season or any glacier. | secondReview: unsure/yes: The approach crosses snow slopes and a ridge from the hut, and nothing found says whether a glacier is touched.

name: Kiss of Death (Sinnes Couloir)
text: [detailed_rack] Conditions are steep snow or neve, with no ice.
[approach] The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season.
earlierWhy: why: It is a steep snow or neve couloir, and the text does not say whether a glacier is on the line.

name: Stanford Route
text: [approach] Climbers start from a high camp at the saddle northeast of the peak, from which a snow ridge rises to a subsummit.
earlierWhy: why: The route climbs a snow ridge from a high camp in a glaciated range, and the search found no glacier detail.

name: East Ridge
text: [hazards] Snow or glacier cover early in the season
[gear] Ice axe and crampons if snow or ice remains
earlierWhy: why: The text mentions snow or glacier cover only for early season. | secondReview: unsure/yes: One report has crampons and pickets on snow and blue ice on the east ridge; glacier cover is not settled.

name: Arete Du Phalanx (Phalanx South Arete)
text: [overview] The initial half is mostly 3rd/4th class, snow or rock, ending at a prominent spire: sling it, then either rappel or downclimb, and cross steep snow rightward.
[overview] Beyond, the narrow aesthetic arete (low 5th) can be bypassed by an easier traverse, up and to the right across steep snow.
[overview] The final ridge brings further steep snow plus easy mixed ground.
earlierWhy: why: The route crosses steep snow in places, and glacier was not checked.

name: Northeast Buttress (Up In Smoke)
text: [overview] The lower buttress takes roughly 16 to 18 pitches of rock at mid-5th standard (up to 5.7) on the crest's left side, ending at the mid-height snowpatch.
[overview] Three pitches climb the lowest ice arete, which is low-angle and likely just snow early in the season;
earlierWhy: why: The buttress is on a peak beside the Monarch Icefield and ends at a mid-height snowpatch, but I found no description of the approach.

name: Austrian Arete
text: [overview] One to two pitches short of the summit area the arete flattens (4th class and some snow).
[detailed_rack] carry an axe and crampons for the descent.
earlierWhy: why: Axe and crampons are carried for the descent and snow is on the arete; the glacier question is not settled.

name: Northeast Buttress
text: [overview] Descent is via the Banner-Ritter notch, then a glissade to Lake Catherine.
[overview] Reach the shoulder under the route over snow, starting from the Gem Lakes Trailhead past Thousand Island Lakes.
[approach] From camp, ascend the snowfield up to the shoulder under the climb and transition to the rock there;
[approach] an ice axe is needed on the snow, and crampons if it is frozen hard.
[descent_text] Head down toward the saddle separating Banner from Ritter, where both sides hold snow, so carry an ice axe.
[descent_text] From the saddle, glissade the snow slope below it back toward the lakes.
earlierWhy: why: Axe needed on the snowfield approach and glissade descent; Banner Glacier proximity is unresolved.

name: Standard route
earlierWhy: why: No route text and no verified facts about this line. | secondReview: no/no: A rock route above Sam Mack Meadow that does not cross the Palisade Glacier.

name: Standard route
earlierWhy: why: No route text and no verified facts about this line. | secondReview: no/no: The name is misleading, and the Class 4 summer line is rock with no active glacier.

name: Antichrist Dihedral
text: [what_to_bring] crampons — may help if snow lies at the base
[approach] From the lake it is about an hour up to the Main Wall, a north-facing wall above the Lilliput Glacier.
earlierWhy: why: Wall sits above the Lilliput Glacier and crampons may help at the base; the approach over it is not settled. | secondReview: unsure/yes: The approach goes to a wall above a named glacier, and I could not confirm whether it is crossed.

name: East Couloir
text: [overview] Beneath the Matterhorn Glacier, the East Couloir is the higher of two ways onto the East Ridge.
[overview] Expect good snow in winter and a mixed scramble or scree slog by summer.
[approach] Where the trail climbs to a shallow col, leave it for a use trail up the ridge east of the glacier drainage to a small lake just under 10,000 feet, which has several campsites.

[approach] Continue up the moraine ridge to the toe of the Matterhorn Glacier, cross its short, nearly flat lower edge, and contour to the East Couloir, the higher of two ways onto the east ridge, in the gap on the left side of the peak.

[descent_text] The normal way down is the approach route: reverse the couloir (snow in winter and spring, loose scree and a mixed scramble by late summer), cross the glacier edge and drop the moraine ridge to the lake and the Horse Creek Trail.
[descent_text] Carry an axe and crampons while the couloir holds snow.
earlierWhy: why: Couloir is a snow route in winter and spring; the route crosses the edge of the small Matterhorn Glacier, hazard not settled.

name: Ski Dreams
earlierWhy: why: Couloir is a snow route in winter and spring; the route crosses the edge of the small Matterhorn Glacier, hazard not settled.

name: Warning Shot (NW Face)
text: [what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — early season, for ice
earlierWhy: why: Ice route that is climbed in the early snow season; no glacier on the line. | secondReview: unsure/yes: The NW face rises above the Mills Glacier side and nothing describes the approach.

name: Dana Couloir
text: [overview] Roughly 1,000 ft of 40-degree snow and ice, a friendly introduction to gully ice.
[what_to_bring] crampons and ice axe — needed early in the season
earlierWhy: why: A 40-degree snow and ice couloir; nearby Dana Glacier involvement is not settled.
